evidence: I read the diff. The new test injects a member named x plus seven backticks plus y into the first reply.

The refusal text echoes the member name as written. jsonstrict.CheckKnownFields returns fmt.Errorf("unknown %s field %q"), and reviewresult/wire.go:159 wraps that error with ErrUnknownMember. %q does not escape backticks.
The injected name is the only unknown member, so it is the one reported. ErrUnknownMember is in shapeRefusals, so Launch re-asks.
reAsk at launch.go:126 builds the fence from longestBacktickRun of the quoted refusal plus 1, with a minimum of 3. The echoed run is 7, so the fence is 8.

The test asserts that the re-ask opens with a fence of 8 backticks, that the echoed run is inside the fence, that the same fence closes it followed by "Reply again", and that text remains after the closing fence.
A fixed three-backtick fence would fail the strings.Cut on the opening fence, so the test pins the behavior.
The test calls the public Launch through launchWorld and inspects the brief the reviewer received. It uses no internals.
The test reads clearly. Its doc comment states the property, and the failure messages print the whole tail.
I did not run the tests.
